title: Landmine Rotation
summary: A loaded rotation that swings a landmine bar from hip to hip, training the obliques to make and resist rotation.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: landmine attachment; barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for obliques (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly obliques total.
Library rating 0.5 for abs (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly abs total.
Library rating 0.3 for front delts (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.2 for glutes: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly glutes total.

setup.text: Hold the end of the bar overhead at arm's length with both hands, feet wider than your hips.
Rotate your torso and pivot your back foot to bring the bar down to one hip.
Reverse the arc through the top and down to the other side.

form_cues.cue: Rotate the bar toward one hip
Move through the torso with arms long
Move from the ribcage and hips together. Keep the arms long.

mistakes.text: Bending the arms so the arms do the work.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: One side at a time, More technical, Finishes overhead.
